title: atlax nameplate (atlax/plant.yaml)
description: The nameplate of one artifact (proposition 1): its id, owner and the norm version it follows. One per artifact repo, at atlax/plant.yaml; copied unchanged to artifacts/<artifact>/plant.yaml in the atlax repo on publish. Writer: the artifact's FSE (Hephaistos for agent-mailbox-api). Readers: `atlax verify`, `atlax publish` (the folder name), `atlax check` (resolves ext:<artifact>), atlax-agent. Samples: plant.sample.yaml, plant-extract.sample.yaml, plant-contracts.sample.yaml, published/agent-mailbox-api/plant.yaml.

artifact.description: The artifact id: its repo slug. Names artifacts/<artifact>/ in the atlax repo and is the <artifact> of every ext:<artifact>#<designation>. Never reused.

owner.description: The seat that owns the slice (the artifact's FSE).

norm.description: The Atlas norm version followed, quoted ("0.1"). A reader refuses a norm it does not know.

purpose.description: One line: what the artifact is for.

repo.description: Where its code lives (host/owner/name); PUBLISHED repeats it.

short.description: The <short> of the artifact's fn: designations (record for agent-mailbox-record, mailbox for agent-mailbox-api; atlax-tool-followups-2 V7). `atlax derive` and the Wails and CLI extractors use it (it wins over overrides.yaml short); absent, they drop a leading `agent-` from the artifact. `atlax verify` and `derive` warn on an element whose fn: designation uses another short.

contracts.description: Where the contract samples of another repo come from (atlax-tool-followups-2 V3, V4), so `atlax verify` reads them by a rule, not from whichever sibling checkout happens to sit beside the artifact: CONTRACTS_DIR on the factory (that repo's contracts/ directory, or its root) when set, else remote at ref. Neither: verify keeps the sibling-checkout message. Sample: plant-contracts.sample.yaml.

repo.description: The contract.repo of the elements it serves (specs).

remote.description: A git remote (URL or path) holding that repo; fetched into the factory's atlax cache.

ref.description: The branch or tag read at the remote; default main.

route_scopes.description: The path, in that repo, of the artifact's route-scope contract (contracts/auth.json: routes.scoped method, path, scope; developer_only and no_token_at_the_api unscoped). `atlax verify` warns when an http element's scope differs from it.

c4_system.description: The c4-map node id of the system this artifact realizes, so derived/map.json and the elements join.

extract.description: What the extractors are told about this artifact's code (atlax-tool-followups U5). Read by `atlax verify`, `touches`, `derive` and `publish`. Sample: plant-extract.sample.yaml.

go_route_wrappers.description: The artifact's own route registration functions, as written at the call (`rt.scoped`, `register`): the first argument is a Go 1.22 mux pattern, read like mux.HandleFunc's. A pattern built `m+" /path"` inside `for _, m := range []string{...}` is one route per value.

exclude.description: Repo-relative directories or files the extractors never read (test-helper packages, such as a fake OIDC issuer).

test.description: How `atlax verify` runs this artifact's named tests (atlax-tool-followups U8). ATLAX_TEST_CMD, when set, still wins.

go_tags.description: Build tags passed to `go test -tags=<a,b>`, so a test behind a build tag (//go:build integration) is run, not read as missing.

cmd.description: A command (sh -c, in the repo) run instead of go test, as ATLAX_TEST_CMD: ATLAX_TEST_PATH, ATLAX_TEST_NAME, ATLAX_TEST_RUN in its environment; exit 0 pass, 5 no such test, else fail.
